_comment_top: Bookstore Platform — Part 15 ch.09 sample breakglass IAM policy. Attached to the `breakglass-emergency` IAM role. The role is assumable ONLY through Vault's AWS secrets engine, after an MFA login, for a 1-hour session; every API call is logged to CloudTrail; every assumption should post an alert to #bookstore-platform-audit. This is the BROAD-admin policy (not full admin) for ESCAPE HATCH use — invoked when a P0 incident exceeds what the standard platform-engineer role can do (e.g. an IAM lockout, a Vault outage, a need to delete a managed resource Crossplane refuses to delete). DO NOT use this as a daily-driver policy; the entire ch.15.09 'breakglass became normal' anti-pattern is what this file is trying to prevent. IAM policy grammar has no comment element, so strip the _comment keys before attaching this document: jq 'walk(if type == "object" then with_entries(select(.key | startswith("_comment") | not)) else . end)' breakglass-iam-policy.json > policy.json
_comment_audit_requirements: Every assumption of this role MUST: (1) be preceded by a Slack declaration in #bookstore-platform-status with an approver, (2) generate a CloudTrail event automatically forwarded to #bookstore-platform-audit, (3) be followed within 24h by the cleanup-after-breakglass.md checklist (rotate, review, postmortem).
_comment_scope_warning: This policy intentionally grants `*` on most services. The trade-off: the breakglass role is for SITUATIONS UNFORESEEN; a narrower policy that doesn't cover the unforeseen case defeats the purpose. The defence against abuse is not the policy scope; it's the auditing (CloudTrail + 24h cleanup) and the assumption gate (Vault login with MFA + Slack approval).

Statement._comment_regions: ap-south-1 is the platform stack's default region (terraform/variables.tf). It was missing from this list, so the escape hatch could not touch the default deployment. Keep this list equal to the regions you actually run in.

Statement._comment_iam_scope: IAM repair is for when the platform locked itself out (a Crossplane composition that broke its own role, an IRSA trust policy pointing at the wrong OIDC provider). It is limited to roles named bookstore-platform-* (the stack's <cluster_name>- prefix at its default) and excludes roles tagged critical=true. Every IAM role terraform/ creates carries that prefix except one: the system managed node group's role, which the EKS module names system-eks-node-group-<random> (renaming it would replace the node group). This statement cannot repair that role; add its ARN here if you want it to. The Karpenter controller role used the sub-module default KarpenterController-<random> until karpenter.tf named it <cluster_name>-karpenter-controller. That tag condition only protects roles that HAVE the tag: StringNotEquals is true when the key is absent, so tag the root admin, audit and breakglass roles. Residual risk, reviewed in cleanup-after-breakglass.md Step 5: on a platform role, AttachRolePolicy can still add any managed policy except the three denied below, and UpdateAssumeRolePolicy can let an outside principal assume the role. Either change outlives the session, so every AttachRolePolicy and UpdateAssumeRolePolicy event from a breakglass session must be reviewed.

Statement._comment_keys: Deactivating or deleting a leaked access key is incident CONTAINMENT. Creating keys is not, and is denied below.

Statement._comment_kms_scope: KMS access is needed for emergency decrypt of secrets stored in S3/RDS. NOT granted: kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion and kms:DeleteAlias (the breakglass role MUST NOT be able to permanently destroy keys; a P0 incident is not a justification for non-recoverable damage).

Statement._comment_trail_read_only: READ ONLY on CloudTrail. The breakglass role MUST NOT be able to disable or delete the trail itself; tampering with the audit log is a security event by itself. The trail is managed by the org-level admin role (out of scope for breakglass).

Statement._comment_explicit_deny: Explicit Deny — defends against the implied Allow from a future wildcard policy that might be attached. The breakglass role is incomplete WITHOUT this Deny — auditability is a non-negotiable property.

Statement._comment_org_scope: Breakglass does NOT extend to AWS Organizations / Billing — that is the parent-account admin role's scope. Locking out an organisation is a multi-day recovery; the breakglass role MUST NOT have that blast radius.

Statement._comment_audit_buckets: The audit + backup buckets are off-limits even for breakglass. A P0 incident is not a justification for deleting backups or disabling replication on the audit log — the backup IS what makes recovery possible.

Statement._comment_tamper: The audit and backup stores accept no deletes, overwrites or configuration changes from breakglass. This is an explicit Deny because BreakglassS3FullAccess matches these buckets through the bookstore-platform-* prefix. Recovery writes go through the owning system's own role.

Statement._comment_k8s_persistence: A new access entry, access-policy association or pod identity association outlives the one-hour session, the same way a new IAM user does. BreakglassFullAdminEC2AndEKS allows eks:*, so these actions are denied explicitly. Any cluster access the breakglass role needs must exist before the incident.

Statement._comment_persistence: The 1-hour TTL is the breakglass role's main safety property, and each action here defeats it: a new user, access key, login profile or role, or a rewritten managed policy, outlives the session. An earlier version ALLOWED iam:CreateAccessKey, CreatePolicy, CreatePolicyVersion, SetDefaultPolicyVersion, AttachRolePolicy and UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on every untagged role, which is a one-step path to permanent admin. Explicit Deny, like DenyCloudTrailManagement, so a future wildcard attachment cannot re-open it. TagRole/UntagRole are denied so the session cannot strip critical=true from a protected role.

Statement._comment_admin_attach: Repairing a platform role never needs AdministratorAccess; attaching it would turn a scoped IRSA role into a standing admin.

_comment_assume_role_policy_separately: This is the PERMISSIONS POLICY. The TRUST POLICY (which principals can assume the role) lives in a separate document. The trust policy MUST require: (a) Vault's IAM principal (the one aws/config/root uses), (b) a maximum session duration of one hour (3600 seconds). MFA is enforced at the Vault login, not in the trust policy: Vault's AssumeRole call carries no MFA context, so an aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition would block Vault itself. Both policies together make the breakglass role complete.
_comment_what_this_does_not_grant: Intentionally not granted: organizations:*, aws-portal:*, billing:*, marketplace:*, cloudtrail:Delete*/Stop*/Update*, and any action that creates a new user, access key, login profile, role, policy or identity provider (see DenyIAMPersistence), and no new EKS access entry, access-policy association or pod identity association (see DenyKubernetesAccessPersistence). Not closed: changes to the EXISTING bookstore-platform-* roles. AttachRolePolicy (any managed policy but the three in DenyAttachingAdminEquivalentPolicies) and UpdateAssumeRolePolicy on those roles are allowed, because repairing a locked-out IRSA role needs them, and both outlive the session. That is why the cleanup checklist reviews every such event. The breakglass role is for OPERATIONAL emergencies, not for organisational changes; the latter requires a different escalation path (the AWS Organizations root account with two-person rule).
